findings_qualitative.value: Dust emission is more compact than stellar mass irrespective of sSFR; SMG stellar sizes and densities match z=1.5 quiescent galaxies

evidence.quote: This ratio does not change with specific star-formation rate (sSFR) over the factor of 30 spanned by our targets

why_this_method.value: Optical light is affected by dust, so color-based M/L corrections recover the underlying mass distribution

evidence.quote: it is possible to recover the underlying stellar mass distributions of galaxies and search for radial gradients in color and hence M/L [∗]

limitations_admitted.value: Foreground dust screen assumption means mass maps are a lower limit to central mass; sample biased to optically bright SMGs

evidence.quote: Due to the high central column densities of dust in our SMGs, our mass distributions likely represent a lower limit to the true central mass density.

referee_caveats_inferred: Small sample (14 high-resolution) with heterogeneous ALMA resolutions
M/L from single color with 0.2-0.5 dex systematic uncertainty
Image-plane fits of low-S/N ALMA data; 3 AS2UDS sources near beam size
Optically bright selection biases against heavily obscured SMGs
